caption: The drawing depicts a square frame composed of wood-effect beams, colored in various shades of brown. The frame is constructed with four straight edges, each bordered by two parallel strips of wood. Between these strips on each edge, there are five identical, evenly spaced, vertical wooden spindles that are symmetrically shaped with three bulbous sections per spindle; these spindles are also colored in brown but with subtle tonal variations to suggest depth. The central opening of the frame is irregular, with slightly bowed or wavy lines on all four sides. The background is a flat, solid off-white or beige color, contrasting with the darker hues of the wooden frame. There is a small, thin signature or inscription in the lower right corner of the image.
title: Zoar Picture Frame
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
